A garden is defined by its contents and its borders. Without deciding what you want in the garden, it ceases to be a garden, and likewise, if you don't maintain its edges, the chaos of nature will see it invaded with undesirable weeds. It ceases to be a garden. The essence of the matter is control. What's important? Where are its edges? How do we defend those boundaries? What threatens it? If you do not go into the task with answers to these questions, you may start well, but you'll invariably fail.

A garden is a lot like a nation. The rudimentary lessons of civics are as simple as tending your first plot. We must define our values. Decide what's important. Decide where our boundaries are, and defend them. Without this, we cease to be. The chaos of nature will infiltrate, and your is lost. Before long, you're unrecognizable from the desperate and chaotic undergrowth where your shovel made its first cut.

A gardener knows that all plants aren't equal. Some are fruitful. Others are simply predatory and opportunistic. Likewise, not all people or values are equal. Like the garden, America defined its borders. It established what it wanted as its contents, its values. These values determine what is fruitful and productive, versus what is predatory and unproductive. It's borders tell us where those values begin, where they end, and the line in the dirt beyond which we don't tolerate encroachment.

Surely, in solidarity, we can help tend to the gardens of others. We can offer advice. We can offer our work and our sweat in a cooperative effort to see everyone cultivate their own, unique gardens. But if/when another gardener allows his plot to spoil, we cannot permit his weeds to foul our own spaces, for we depend on the fruit of our garden, and everyone's soil is ultimately their own.

The American garden works. It's proven that it works. We fought bravely to show the rest of the world our concept worked. If you don't like the American garden, what we've decided to cultivate here, or the borders we defend to preserve it, get the fuck out. There is a large segment of our population, perhaps for loss of this connection to the earth, to our roots, for whom these concepts are lost. Their arrogance and privilege betray their better sense. As they observe the discord outside, they don't recognize that our values and borders are the intervening force which gives them that orderly, safe space to look on from. They actively invite weeds, the tumult, and lawlessness. These are the fruits of a spoiled garden. Any gardener that invites the weeds desires no fruit, and this is not a beneficial partner.

It should be no surprise that the majority of America's farmers are conservatives. They're involved in the civics of common sense all of the time. When your life depends on your garden, and it has brought you plenty, you understand clearly the foolishness of protesting the way you tend it.
